instruction.what: Step 2.1, the structure of one subgroup (stage 1, B3): what stands with the subgroup's words in each verse, read from the stored structure. One item at a time: double-meaning (a surface with more than one code), qualifier (negators and the word each reaches, adjectives, adverbs, prepositional qualifiers), entity (who is named or referred to), direction (from whom to whom, by the grammar), pairing (one row for each partner collection: its words in the verses shared with the subgroup). Nothing here says what anything does for the inner being; that begins at step 3.1.
read: Take one row at a time (`rows`): what it asks, its occurrences (`as`: member, the subgroup's word; partner, the other word), and its verses.

Read each verse (`verses`) from its stored structure, one line for each word: * marks an occurrence of the subgroup; then the position, surface, Strong's code and morph, and what the pairing makes of the word (its type, the qualifier it carries, a negator, a party, the collections of a word of another collection). Nothing is evaluated that is not stored.
Where each word stands: its side and distance from the subgroup's word, from the positions. Adjacency is not scope: a negator or qualifier is read for the word it reaches by the grammar.
A pairing row shows the WordNet control for its partner collection: a pairing WordNet gives and the verses do not show is one to look for; a pairing only the verses show has no control.
Differences in meaning are read from the base data (the Strong's code, the morph, the construction), not from the English alone. The subgroup's 1.1 senses (`senses`) are what the findings build on.
write: Fill `answer.rows`: for each row, disposition observed with its `findings`, or none with its `reason` (where the row allows none: nothing of the item stands with the subgroup in its verses).

One finding for each distinct thing the structure shows; the same finding in several verses is ONE finding naming all its occurrences; a verse that shows something different is its own finding. Together the findings name every occurrence of the row (occurrence ids or verse references), each in one finding.

kind: as the template gives it (pairing; relation for direction; face for double-meaning). obs_text: concise; names the verses it holds in, as the package writes the references (for example Act 18:4); states what the structure shows (which word, where it stands, what it reaches or gives by the grammar); never a verse restated, never what it does for the inner being.
basis: stated (the verse says it) or read (read from the structure), with `grounds`: words copied exactly from the verses it is tied to (the record checks them).
Each subgroup's surface has its own finding; none joins two subgroups. A data error is named in grounds, not fixed.

`older`: answer each older observation shown under the row, once: keep (with `nature`), restate (with `nature`, `new_text`, `checked`), merge (with `into`), consume (with `carriers` ["this"] or observation ids, and `mapping`), delete_neither (with `reason`), carry (with `to` and `reason`), defer (with `collection`, `nature`, `finding`). One listed under another row is answered there.
Where a reading, sense, enrichment or finding holds every occurrence of the row's subject, `occurrences` may be "all": the recorder names them.

Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action CheckAnswer -File <the answer file>: every problem at once, each with its rule, nothing written; correct the answer until it finds none, then -Action RecordStructure -File <the answer file>. The record refuses the whole file on any fault and lists every fault.

keep.text: Morph is read, not carried: where occurrences of a word show different stems or voices, record whether the subject does, undergoes or causes the act.

A word that is only a homonym or a name, with no meaningful context, is recorded as such (tag no-human-context) and left. Data errors found while reading are flagged (tag data-error), not fixed in the reading.

A word is read per its lettered Strong's code (its grain), never the bare lemma (B:113). The occurrences of a word with several senses are related per grain and never aggregated across grains: related verses are same-grain occurrences.
One observation per finding, never a duplicate description; a finding applying to several verses or words carries several nodes, each with the word's role in it.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Where the evidence points to more than one reading, each is its own observation with its own evidence.
A re-read includes the observations already recorded for the verse, so the reading sees prior findings and builds on them.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

Every older live observation with a live node on an occurrence of the row (a stage that is not the build's own) is answered in fill.older when the row is recorded, once: keep or restate (each with its marker), merge into a named observation, consume (live observations carry its meaning, stated in words, verified before it is deleted), delete as neither (comment first), or defer to a named collection (marked now; only the finding is left to that collection). An observation already marked by the validation, answered in a build or deferred is not asked again. A new observation whose text equals that of another live observation of the collection is refused, the other named. LayerCheck re-derives both from the tables. The end state of a collection's build is that every observation of its scope is marked and fixed or deleted, every word node complete or with its reason, and each deferral owned by a named collection.

When a verse is worked, every existing observation and node on it, of any stage, is checked against the verse by its wording. The stage is not an indication of the nature of an observation and is never used to filter. Each observation is accepted, modified (changed in place; the old value, the new value and the reason are kept in ib_observation_change), soft deleted (the `deleted` column, with the reason), merged (a duplicate description, into the observation that is kept) or, when its wording shows it is not verse understanding, left exactly as it is with the reason. The check's fixes are part of it and need no separate approval. Nothing is physically deleted.

The nodes of a layer observation are the occurrences the aspect demands (a word's occurrences, the group's occurrences, the partner's occurrences in the verses they share), written by the recorder with the collection and the subgroup of each surface; they are never typed. An item answered by senses (word-sense) names, for each sense, the occurrences it holds for, and together the senses cover every occurrence; the recorder checks them against the data. The interpretation is the observation text, founded in what the evidence shows (basis stated or read, B:131) and tied to its verses (the text names them and does not restate them): the items of every step (S1, 1.1, 1.2, 2.1) state what the dictionary, the verses and the stored structure show of a word and never what a word does for the inner being; their nodes carry the role lexical and no route. The whole file is checked and written in one transaction; any problem refuses all of it. A row answered again withdraws its earlier observations with the reason.

An aspect is recorded as none only where its item allows it (cfg_setting layer.reading none_allowed) and with its reason in words. A group definition and a group's Strong's enrichment are always observed.

A node is on one occurrence (verse_lexical_id) and carries the collection of its surface (a supportive node, the collection of the surface it supports); a node already on the observation for the same occurrence is not written twice, and takes the role. A node with no collection to carry, or on a verse out of scope (B:130), is not written and is listed.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

Every live observation marked inner_being holds at least one live traced node on a live observation marked evidence, or on a live inner-being observation that itself traces to evidence (the trace chain of stage 4: a 3.2 behaviour traces the 3.1 elements it gathers, a 3.3 match the 3.1 and 3.2 observations it comes from; at most three links), unless it is recorded self-evidencing: it quotes its verse in full and holds a word node for every word it relies on. A traced node never points at a deleted observation. A trace points first at existing evidence; an evidence observation is created only when none states the fact and it states what the nodes and the quotation do not. An inner-being observation traced to evidence not yet marked is pending, not failed.

A step of the layered reading opens only when the grouping is finished (every surface placed in a subgroup or isolated with its reason, every subgroup holding a surface) and the previous step is closed; with -Subgroup the needs and gates are judged for that subgroup alone (#2538). Step S1 is read after the grouping; step 1.1 needs step S1 closed: every word of the subgroup (surface and lettered Strong's code) answered and validated. Opening derives one ledger row for each aspect the data demands (cfg_setting layer.reading); an aspect the data no longer demands is retired, a new one is added, and a second open changes nothing.

A read or record command names a live collection, a live subgroup of it where the read is by subgroup, and a step or item the layered reading knows. A command that names one that does not exist is refused and writes nothing.

An answer is the output form its read wrote: the `command` of that read; every entry an object, or a list, where the form has one; each field in its place with its type (a key unique in the answer, a text, a reason in words); each item answered once; and at least one entry where the form asks for entries. A file in another shape is refused whole and nothing is written.

Every ledger row, occurrence, observation, sense, node, verse and collection an answer names is one the packet offered for this unit, or a key the answer itself defines, and is live in the database. A name outside them is refused.

Every coded value of an answer (kind, basis, item, part, role, route, mode, polarity, flag type, disposition, verdict, action, nature, stage, status) is one of the values the configuration allows for it (cfg_enum, cfg_setting layer.reading, reading.observation_items, validate.reading), as the packet lists them. Any other value is refused.

A read or record runs only where the ledger has its unit at that step: the row open, or answered and not yet validated, and the steps before it closed (S1 before 1.1; the 2.1 rows before the sweep; the sweep before the evidence validation; its gate before 3.1; every subgroup through 3.1 before 3.2). Out of order it is refused, and the message names what comes first.

A read writes its packet within the time and size the configuration sets (cfg_setting layer.read_types: limits, package_max_chars, read_max_seconds). A read that would exceed them is refused, nothing is written, and the limit is named.

The code of the reading runs only where the configuration it reads is in place (the settings, steps, items, natures, enums and rules it names). Where the code is ahead of the configuration, the command is refused and names what is missing.

Record the parties: who bears the act, who causes it, who is acted on (source, target, impact, purpose), and the route (cfg_enum observation_route), whose meaning is cfg_behaviour_rule 72 (route-verses-hib-other-beings-data-only): A another being in its own right, B another being with the human inner being, C no bearing, data only; a verse may take A and B. A non-human being is never itself a HIB; a collective stays one HIB; an implied party is named as referential, never asserted.
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.

An observation is created with its marker (ib_observation.nature, from the item answered, cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature; a finding file never sets it) and every word node with the columns of layer.reading node_required. A column the data cannot give (layer.reading node_gap_columns: an empty morph in the source row, a surface with no placement in the collection index) is left empty and its reason is kept on the node (disposition_note); any other missing column refuses the whole file and nothing is written. A trace to a deleted observation is refused (IB-07).

A lookup of related data in the build or the validation is by an indexed column and takes a chunk of ids (cfg_setting layer.scan chunk); none runs once for each item of a list, and a statement that uses more work than layer.scan max_vm_ops is stopped and named, nothing written (lib/scanguard.py). The tests refuse a statement of the build whose query plan scans a table (layer.scan scan_ok lists the temporary tables a statement may scan).

Evidence states what the data are or show, tied to a verse. Inner being states how something works in the inner being, based on evidence, a building block of the stage 5 claims. The marker (ib_observation.nature) follows the content and purpose of the observation, never its stage (RS-04): an observation of any stage may be inner being when it traces to evidence. One that states both is split. The marker is set when the observation is created, by the item that is answered (cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature); a finding file never sets it; the validation changes it only where the content shows the item's nature does not hold.

senses.text: Exertion toward a goal: effort spent to reach or to do something, in 1Th 2:17, Gal 2:17, Luk 13:24, 1Ti 4:10, Heb 12:14, 1Cor 14:12, Heb 4:11 and Ecc 2:22; the goal is named in each, a meeting, a standing before God, entry, peace and holiness, excelling, rest, or in Ecc 2:22 the labour itself.

Contention against an opponent: disputing with another or rousing oneself against another, in Isa 45:9 against one's maker, in Pro 28:4 by those who keep the law against the wicked, and in Isa 41:11 where Israel's opponents are named by their dispute with Israel.
Physical fighting: a bodily fight between men in Exo 21:22 and warfare between peoples in Psa 60:1, both with the verb natsah.
Jacob's contending with God: the struggle with God, or with the angel, in which Jacob prevailed, told in Gen 32:28, Hos 12:3 and Hos 12:4 with sarah and sur.

A reaching after wind: in Ecc 1:14, Ecc 1:17, Ecc 2:11, Ecc 2:17, Ecc 2:26, Ecc 4:4, Ecc 4:6, Ecc 4:16 and Ecc 6:9 two related nouns, reut and rayon, name a striving after wind, a reaching after what gives nothing to hold.

rows.asks: Does this surface carry a different Strong's code or sense in different verses (the faces of the word)? State the codes and the verses.

findings.obs_text: In Exo 21:22 the surface strive stands on two codes at one position: natsah (H5327A, struggle, Niphal) and ki (H3588A, the conjunction 'when'), so the one English word holds both the opening conjunction and the verb of a fight between men.

In Pro 28:4 (garah, H1624, a Hithpael verb) and Isa 41:11 (rib, H7379, a noun in construct) the surface strive stands on two Hebrew codes of contention, each followed by the party opposed, 'them' and 'you'.

In Luk 13:24, 1Ti 4:10, 1Cor 14:12, Heb 4:11 and Heb 12:14 the surface strive stands on four Greek codes, agonizomai (G0075), zeteo (G2212), spoudazo (G4704) and dioko (G1377), each with a goal as an infinitive or an object: one English word covers struggle, seeking, eagerness and pursuit.

older.new_text: In 1Cor 14:12 the seeking rendered 'strive' is done by the readers addressed and is aimed at excelling in building up the church.
older.checked: the verse text of 1Cor 14:12 and its stored structure: yourselves G5210, strive G2212 V-PAM-2P, excel G4052, building G3619, church G1577
older.reason: Carried here from S1: its finding of who acts and toward what stands, but it named a cluster by a bare code (M44) and called the church a party of an operation; restated as what the verse shows.

findings.obs_text: In Ecc 1:14, 2:11, 2:17, 2:26, 4:4, 4:6 and 6:9 (reut, H7469) and in Ecc 1:17 and 4:16 (rayon, H7475) the surface striving stands in the same construct phrase with 'wind', so the two codes give one face in that phrase.

In Ecc 2:22 striving stands on rayon (H7475) in construct with 'heart' and joined to 'toil', with no 'wind': the code that gives the phrase with wind in Ecc 1:17 and 4:16 here names the effort of the heart in labour.

older.new_text: Ecc 6:9 calls the wandering of the appetite (nephesh) vanity and a striving after wind, set after the sight of the eyes, which it says is better.
older.checked: the verse text of Ecc 6:9 and its stored structure: wandering H1980I, appetite H5315L, vanity H1892, striving H7469, wind H7307H
older.reason: Carried here from S1: its finding, appetite and the striving after wind in one verse, stands, but it quoted the whole verse under a label (B:131); restated in words of its own.

findings.obs_text: In Psa 60:1 the surface strove stands on natsah (H5327A, a Hiphil infinitive) for David's warfare against Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, in the superscription.

In Hos 12:3 (sarah, H8280, with God) and Hos 12:4 (sur, H7786, with the angel) the surface strove stands on two different codes for the one struggle of Jacob, told in two lines that follow each other.
